strategy: SPY at-the-money straddle debit observed ahead of scheduled CPI/FOMC releases

pre_registration.events: Hardcoded CPI/FOMC calendar dates in config_2x.yaml's options_experiments.event_volatility.events, through 2026-12-10.

hypothesis: Implied break-even move priced into the ATM straddle ahead of a scheduled macro release can be compared, after the fact, to the realized move — a volatility-premium question, distinct from and not requiring any directional view.
known_gaps: The event calendar is a fixed list of dates, not a live feed — it silently stops producing observations after 2026-12-10 with no error, no CRITICAL line, and no cron-visible signal. Whoever next extends config_2x.yaml's events list should treat 'no observations in a while' as potentially this, not necessarily a broken collector (see scripts/weekly.py's summarize_event_volatility_shadow, which checks staleness against the most recent observation rather than a rolling window for exactly this reason).

The observation window is inclusive of the event day itself (0 <= days_to_event <= window), so an observation taken after a pre-market release has already happened would still be recorded as 'ahead of' that event unless the collector happens to run only pre-market that day. Worth double-checking before treating a same-day observation as a true pre-event snapshot.
promotion_policy: A recorded observation is quote/price data only and can never submit an order.

Review after at least 20 observations spanning at least four independent scheduled events, given how sparse the calendar is (a handful of CPI/FOMC dates per quarter) — a much longer collection period than the near-daily shadows.
No paper-active path is defined yet; this shadow exists to determine whether event-conditioned implied vol is even mispriced relative to realized moves before any strategy is designed around it.
limitations: The free indicative options feed modifies quotes and may not represent an executable OPRA market.
A single straddle snapshot says nothing about the realized move until the event has actually occurred and been observed separately.
The event list requires manual maintenance; it is not sourced from a calendar API.
